title: Normalize and validate a user record
description: Implement normalize_user_record(record). Validate a user record dict and return a normalized copy with exactly the keys 'name', 'email', 'age', 'tags'. Raise TypeError if record is not a dict. Raise KeyError naming the first missing key if any of 'name', 'email', 'age' is absent. 'name' must be a str (else TypeError); strip it and raise ValueError if it is then empty. 'email' must be a str (else TypeError); strip and lowercase it, then raise ValueError unless it contains exactly one '@' with a non-empty local part and a non-empty domain that contains at least one '.'. 'age' must be an int that is not a bool (else TypeError) and within 0..150 inclusive (else ValueError). Optional 'tags' defaults to []; if present it must be a list of str (TypeError for a non-list or a non-str element); strip each tag, drop empty tags, and remove duplicates keeping first-occurrence order. Extra keys are ignored.
invariants: The return value has exactly the keys 'name', 'email', 'age', 'tags'; extra input keys are dropped.
bool is rejected for 'age' with TypeError even though bool subclasses int.
Email normalization happens before validation: surrounding whitespace is stripped and case is lowered.
Duplicate tags are removed after stripping, preserving first-occurrence order; empty stripped tags are dropped.
KeyError is raised for missing required keys, TypeError for wrong types, ValueError for well-typed but invalid values.
